query.description: Case-insensitive literal substring of an element tag or attribute value (name, label, text, ID, etc.). Searches all element types, including hidden elements. Blank or omitted keeps the default driver-specific filter.

xpathAttributes.description: Additional XPath attribute names in priority order, e.g. AutomationId or data-testid. Tried before built-in attributes; defaults remain as fallback. No namespace prefixes or XPath expressions.

sessionId.description: Session ID; defaults to the active session.

definition.name: generate_locators

definition.description: Boot an iOS/tvOS simulator, download/cache WDA, and launch it on a free per-simulator port. Pass capabilitiesHint (appium:webDriverAgentUrl) to appium_session_management action=create to reuse WDA. skipWda=true only boots. APPIUM_MCP_WDA_APP_PATH can point to an extracted WebDriverAgentRunner-Runner.app (absolute path) to skip download.

udid.description: The UDID of the iOS simulator to prepare. Use select_device to get this.

platform.description: The simulator platform to download WDA for. Default is "ios". Use "tvos" for Apple TV simulators.

skipWda.description: If true, only boot the simulator without downloading or installing WDA. Default: false.

forceRefreshWda.description: If true, re-download WDA even if already cached. Default: false.

definition.name: prepare_ios_simulator

definition.description: Discover/select a LOCAL device. Ask for platform if unknown; one device is auto-selected. For multiple devices, ask the user to choose, then pass deviceUdid. Next: prepare_ios_simulator for iOS simulators, then appium_session_management action=create. Skip for REMOTE servers: pass device capabilities (appium:deviceName/appium:udid) and the user-provided remoteServerUrl to session creation.

platform.description: Platform chosen by the user.

iosDeviceType.description: Required for ios: simulator or real device.

deviceUdid.description: User-selected UDID. Omit to discover devices.

definition.name: select_device

resources.description:
Generate code for the current page with locators which was retrieved from generate_locators tool.
    The code should be generated in the same priorty order as the locators were generated.
    Always use the actions API code from the template for the gestures.
    For iOS the priority order is:
      'id',
      'accessibility id',
      '-ios predicate string',
      '-ios class chain',
      'xpath',
      'class name',
    For Android the priority order is:
       'id',
      'accessibility id',
      'xpath',
      '-android uiautomator',
      'class name',
    which follows the page factory pattern. Dont not strictly create test cases, just generate the code for locators.
resources.name: Generate Code With Locators

bridge_command.description: Override command for the FULU bridge host or macOS/WSL wrapper; defaults to BAMBU_NETWORK_BRIDGE_COMMAND. Per-call overrides require MCP_ALLOW_EXECUTABLE_ARG=1.

bambu_network_config_dir.description: Config/log directory used by the BambuNetwork agent; defaults to BAMBU_NETWORK_CONFIG_DIR or a user config directory.

definition.name: blender_mcp_call
definition.description: Call a discovered tool on the configured Blender MCP server, preserving its full MCP content and errors. Discover tool schemas with blender_mcp_status first; execute_blender_code accepts Python code and user_prompt. Calls can modify the active Blender scene and are never automatically retried.

tool_name.description: Exact name advertised by Blender MCP, such as get_scene_info or execute_blender_code.

arguments.description: Arguments matching the remote tool's discovered input schema. Preserve the user's own words in user_prompt when the remote tool requests it.

timeout_ms.description: Total connection, discovery, and tool deadline in milliseconds; defaults to BLENDER_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 120000.

definition.name: blender_mcp_edit_model
definition.description: Import, edit, and export a local STL through standard Blender MCP with verified output and existing scene objects preserved. Requires a shared local filesystem and Blender Object Mode. Also supports a separately configured legacy executable bridge.

stl_path.description: Path to the local STL file

operations.description: Ordered operations: decimate:<ratio greater than 0 and at most 1>, remesh:<positive voxel size in STL units>, boolean_union:<STL path>. Legacy custom bridges define their own operations.

output_path.description: Required for standard MCP previews and execution: new local STL output path whose parent exists. Existing files are never overwritten. Optional for legacy-only bridge configuration.

user_prompt.description: The user's own words describing the edit, passed unchanged to Blender MCP.

timeout_ms.description: Total Blender request deadline in milliseconds; defaults to BLENDER_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 120000.

bridge_command.description: Legacy custom bridge executable override, not a standard MCP command. Per-call overrides require MCP_ALLOW_EXECUTABLE_ARG=1.

execute.description: Apply edits and export (true) or validate and return the prepared request without connecting (false, default).

definition.name: blender_mcp_setup
definition.description: Check or update the MCP for Blender add-on that the configured Blender bridge (BLENDER_MCP_COMMAND uvx, BLENDER_MCP_ARGS naming mcp-for-blender or blender-mcp) needs. Without update: which add-on file Blender loads, its protocol and the protocol the package expects, whether Blender is listening and the running add-on's own handshake. Changes nothing. With update: true, stages the add-on with the package's own installer (mcp-for-blender install-addon) at the inspected version, checks it, keeps the old file as a backup next to it and renames the new one into place. Never starts, stops or edits Blender; a running Blender uses the new add-on once it is re-enabled or restarted. A custom bridge returns supported false.

update.description: Replace the installed add-on with the package's own (default false: check only).

supported.description: The configured bridge is the upstream MCP for Blender package run with uvx, so this tool can check and update its add-on.

package.description: The package as BLENDER_MCP_ARGS names it.

expected_protocol.description: The add-on protocol the package needs.

listening.description: The add-on answers on BLENDER_HOST:BLENDER_PORT (default localhost:9876): Blender is running with it started.

live.description: The running add-on's get_addon_status (up_to_date, protocol_version, expected_protocol_version, blender_version); null when it has none or it couldn't be read. Only while listening.

live_error.description: Why the running add-on's handshake couldn't be read.

target.description: The add-on file Blender loads (for the running Blender's version, when it reports one).

message.description: What the person can do, in plain words, when the add-on can't be checked or updated here (with reason or target_problem). Clients show it as it is.

current.description: The installed file carries the expected protocol. A running Blender may still have the old add-on loaded: see live.

replaced.description: update: the file was replaced. Blender runs the new add-on once it is re-enabled or Blender restarts.

backup.description: update: the previous add-on file, kept next to it.

definition.name: blender_mcp_status
definition.description: Inspect Blender MCP configuration or connect and discover the remote server's tools and schemas. Connecting does not edit the scene; use get_scene_info through blender_mcp_call to check the Blender addon.

connect.description: Initialize the configured stdio MCP server and discover its tools (default false).

timeout_ms.description: Total connection and discovery deadline in milliseconds; defaults to BLENDER_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 120000.

definition.name: camera_frame
definition.description: Read the shared camera stream, optionally waiting up to 10 seconds. Returns JPEG only when newer than since_seq and visibly changed (32×18 grayscale difference). Retain the last delivered frame's seq on unchanged. max_width resizes JPEG to the viewer. Does not start a stopped stream.

host.description: Printer LAN host or IP; defaults to the configured Bambu host.

bambu_serial.description: Printer serial number; defaults to the configured serial and identifies its shared stream.

bambu_token.description: Printer LAN access code; defaults to the configured access code.

since_seq.description: Sequence of the last delivered JPEG; retain it when a result is unchanged.

wait_ms.description: Maximum time to await a newer changed frame; zero returns immediately.

max_width.description: Optional maximum JPEG width in pixels, preserving aspect ratio and never enlarging.

max_bytes.description: Optional maximum encoded JPEG bytes. Downscales further at quality 70 when needed; base64 adds about one third plus protocol overhead. Use 42000 for a two-second 30 KB/s viewer budget.

changed_only.description: Return JPEG only when its thumbnail differs enough from the last delivered frame.

min_change.description: Minimum mean absolute grayscale thumbnail difference, normalized from zero to one.

definition.name: camera_snapshot
definition.description: Capture a single JPEG frame from the printer's chamber camera. A1/P1 use TCP-on-6000; X1/P2S/H2/X2D use RTSP via ffmpeg. Returns JPEG as base64; pass save_path to also write the bytes to disk.

save_path.description: Optional absolute path to write the JPEG to disk. If omitted, only the base64 payload is returned.

timeout_ms.description: Max ms to wait for a live frame (default 8000). A1/P1 cameras first replay a buffered frame, which is skipped, so a live frame takes about 3 s, longer on cold start.

bambu_model.description: Printer model. Used to route to the correct protocol or fail fast on unsupported models. Defaults to BAMBU_MODEL.

experimental.description: Deprecated and ignored. Earlier this flag let callers probe H2 series via the A1/P1 TCP-on-6000 path; live testing on an H2S confirmed H2 uses RTSP instead, so the flag has no effect now.

ffmpeg_path.description: Override path to the ffmpeg binary used by the RTSP path. Defaults to FFMPEG_PATH or ffmpeg via $PATH. Per-call overrides require MCP_ALLOW_EXECUTABLE_ARG=1. Required only for the RTSP transport (X1, P2S, H2 series, X2D).

host.description: Hostname or IP of the printer (default: value from env)

definition.name: camera_stream_start
definition.description: Start or renew one persistent camera connection for this printer. Call only while watched; it closes automatically after idle_timeout_ms without a viewer request. camera_snapshot then reuses its latest frame. No printer motion or print commands.

host.description: Printer LAN host or IP; defaults to the configured Bambu host.

bambu_serial.description: Printer serial number; defaults to the configured serial and identifies its shared stream.

bambu_token.description: Printer LAN access code; defaults to the configured access code.

bambu_model.description: Bambu model used to select the camera transport; defaults to BAMBU_MODEL.

fps.description: Maximum processed frames per second. The first viewer sets the rate until the stream closes.

idle_timeout_ms.description: Close the shared connection after this many milliseconds without a viewer request.

definition.name: camera_stream_stop
definition.description: Close this printer's camera connection and free its cached frames. Other printers keep their own streams. Active viewers may restart it; normally let the idle timeout close a shared stream.

host.description: Printer LAN host or IP; defaults to the configured Bambu host.

bambu_serial.description: Printer serial number; defaults to the configured serial and identifies its shared stream.

bambu_token.description: Printer LAN access code; defaults to the configured access code.

definition.name: cancel_print
definition.description: Cancel the current print job on the Bambu Lab printer

host.description: Hostname or IP of the printer (default: value from env)

connection_mode.description: The connection the print used. Defaults to BAMBU_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_MODE, the same default print_3mf uses, else the model's route.

connection_type.description: FULU BambuNetwork connection type the print used. Defaults to BAMBU_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_TYPE, as for print_3mf. Authenticated controls support lan.

definition.name: clear_hms_errors

host.description: Hostname or IP of the printer (default: value from env)

definition.name: counterpart_discover_printers
definition.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): Bambu printers on the local network, from their own SSDP announcements (UDP 2021), with serial, model (as bambu_model names it), name and firmware. Listens for duration_ms (default 4000). network is "unavailable" when another app holds the port. Never connects to or authenticates with a printer.

definition.name: counterpart_make_3mf
definition.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): combine STL parts exported separately (for example each body of a design) into one new 3MF for multi-colour printing. The parts keep their relative positions as one assembly, and each part prints with its filament number (default: part 1 uses filament 1, part 2 filament 2, and so on). Slice it with slice_stl, passing one load_filaments profile per filament number, then print it with print_3mf and ams_mapping or ams_slots. Never overwrites a file.

stl_path.description: Path to the part's STL file.

name.description: The part's name, shown in the slicer.

filament.description: 1-based project filament for this part; defaults to the part's position (1, 2, ...).

out_path.description: New .3mf path whose parent directory exists. Existing files are never overwritten.

path.description: Absolute path of the written 3MF.

filaments.description: Highest filament number any part uses; pass that many load_filaments to slice_stl.

definition.name: counterpart_print_progress
definition.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): the printer's state, current job (name, task id, percent, time left, layers, stage words), temperatures, active filament and problems with Bambu's HMS messages and links. Read from the MQTT report this server keeps, so a held session asks the printer nothing; observedAt is when the printer sent it. An unreachable printer reports state offline. Read-only; not a safety check.

bambu_model.description: Printer model; defaults to BAMBU_MODEL. Used for the chamber sensor and Bambu's per-model messages.

host.description: Hostname or IP of the printer (default: value from env)

observedAt.description: When the printer reported this (MQTT report time), ISO 8601.

definition.name: counterpart_print_route
definition.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): how this server reaches the printer for prints and for Stop/Pause/Resume. route is "lan" (the local network through FULU's BambuNetwork bridge, or the configured X2D native or Bambu Connect mode), "cloud" (Bambu Cloud through FULU's bridge) or "developer" (the local network straight to a printer in LAN Only + Developer Mode, whose Pause, Resume and Stop need no Bambu app). options lists each with its label, whether it can be chosen here (and why not) and what controls do on it; choices lists the ids that can be chosen. mode and type are BAMBU_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_MODE and BAMBU_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_TYPE as resolved. Pass route to change it: the change applies to the next print and control at once, and is saved to the .env file in this server's working directory when that file exists (savedTo; null otherwise). Sends nothing to the printer.

route.description: Change the route. Omit to read it.

definition.name: counterpart_printer_info
definition.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): this server's name and version, the configured Bambu printer, and which progress, layer, camera, filament, pause/resume/cancel and print features it has. Sends nothing to the printer.

bambu_model.description: Printer model; defaults to BAMBU_MODEL. Selects the camera transport.

host.description: Hostname or IP of the printer (default: value from env)

bambu_token.description: Access token (default: value from env); never returned.

definition.name: counterpart_propose_filaments
definition.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): which loaded AMS spool prints each of a model's colours, before slicing. Reads the live AMS once. trays lists the spools a person may choose (label like "A2", a person-readable name, colour, material, feed). proposal gives each filament its nearest spool in OKLab colour with the asked-for material preferred, and a verdict: same-colour, closest (that colour isn't loaded; note says so), no-colour or none. One print feeds from one source. Pass chosen to check the person's spools against what is loaded now; mapping then lists every filament slot's spool (painted slots included), and problems says why a choice can't print.

filaments.description: The model's filaments a person sees, in project order: 1-based index, part name, the colour it belongs in and its material when known.

painted.description: Filament slots no part names (painted regions). Each follows the chosen spools' feed; prints false when the selected plate never uses it.

chosen.description: The person's spool for each filament, in the same order: checked against what is loaded now. Omit for the proposal alone.

sliced.description: The file is already sliced: its materials are fixed, so only spools of the same material qualify.

bambu_model.description: Printer model; defaults to BAMBU_MODEL. Selects the filament profiles that decide which spools can slice.

host.description: Hostname or IP of the printer (default: value from env)

bambu_token.description: Access token (default: value from env); never returned.

definition.name: counterpart_setup_fields
definition.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): the printers this server drives and the settings it reads for each, by .env variable name (first canonical, then aliases): label, hint, whether required, the model choices and the model each serial-number prefix names. Pass serial to get the model it names. Sends nothing to a printer and returns no configured values.

serial.description: A Bambu serial number: model is the one it names, when known.

aliases.description: Older names this server reads before env: a client writing env removes these, or the old value wins.
Older names this server reads before env: a client writing env removes these, or the old value wins.

definition.name: delete_printer_file
definition.description: Delete a file from the Bambu Lab printer's SD card via FTPS. Destructive: requires confirm:true. Restricted to cache/, timelapse/, and logs/ directories. Path traversal segments (..) are rejected.

filename.description: File to delete. Bare names default to cache/<name>; pass a relative path like timelapse/foo.mp4 to target other allowed directories.

confirm.description: Must be true to actually delete. When false or omitted the call returns without sending an FTP request.

host.description: Hostname or IP of the printer (default: value from env)

definition.name: extend_stl_base
definition.description: Extend the base of an STL file by a specified amount

stl_path.description: Path to the STL file to modify

extension_height.description: Height in mm to extend the base by

definition.name: fusion_mcp_call
definition.description: Call a discovered tool on the configured Fusion MCP server, such as create_sketch, extrude, fillet, create_parameter, set_parameter, check_interference or execute_code, preserving its full MCP content and errors. Discover tool schemas with fusion_mcp_status first. Calls change the open Fusion design and are never automatically retried. Most tools need an open design: call fusion_mcp_new_design first.

document_id.description: Session identity returned by a bound new design. Every operation targets this document, even if the user changes tabs.

tool_name.description: Exact tool name advertised by the Fusion MCP server.

arguments.description: Arguments matching the remote tool's discovered input schema.

timeout_ms.description: Total deadline in milliseconds; defaults to FUSION_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 180000.

definition.name: fusion_mcp_export
definition.description: Export the open Fusion design into an existing directory as <name>.stl (export_stl of one body), <name>.f3d (export_f3d) and <name>.parameters.json (its user parameters), and return their absolute paths. The STL is checked as a finite triangle mesh; slice it like any other model. Fusion must run on this computer, and existing files are never overwritten.

document_id.description: Session identity returned by a bound new design. Every operation targets this document, even if the user changes tabs.

output_dir.description: Existing directory for the three files.

name.description: File name without extension, such as bracket.

body_name.description: The body to export as STL. Optional when the design has exactly one body.

timeout_ms.description: Total deadline in milliseconds; defaults to FUSION_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 180000.

boundingBox.description: Measured from the written STL, in its own units: min, max and dimensions.

stlUnits.description: The STL's units, from its size against the Fusion body's.

fusionSizeMm.description: The Fusion body's bounding-box size in mm.

definition.name: fusion_mcp_new_design
definition.description: Open a new parametric design document in Fusion (execute_code with app.documents.add(FusionDesignDocumentType)). The Fusion MCP tools work on the open design, so a design pass calls this first.

bind_document.description: Create an isolated document and return its session identity, restoring the previously active document. Requires document-binding support in the configured bridge/add-in.

source_f3d.description: With bind_document, import this absolute F3D path into a new document for revision.

timeout_ms.description: Total deadline in milliseconds; defaults to FUSION_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 180000.

definition.name: fusion_mcp_setup
definition.description: Check or install what the Fusion bridge needs on macOS: Autodesk Fusion itself (found, never installed), the Fusion360MCP add-in from DMontgomery40/fusion360-mcp-server at 86a3016a5a5b (every file checked against its pinned SHA-256) set to run on startup, a login item that sets FUSION_MCP_PORT for Fusion however it is opened, and this server's FUSION_MCP_* settings. Without install: reports them and changes nothing. With install: true, installs what is missing and adds the missing settings to this server's own .env (after a copy of it), keeping a configured FUSION_MCP_COMMAND and its arguments. Never starts or quits Fusion; check the connection with fusion_mcp_status.

install.description: Install what is missing (default false: check only).

configured.description: FUSION_MCP_COMMAND is set for this server.

env_file.description: The .env this server read at start, when there is one.

ready.description: The add-in is at the pin and runs on startup, the port login item is installed and the bridge is configured. Fusion may still need opening: see fusion_mcp_status.

message.description: When not ready: what is missing and what to do, in plain words. Clients show it as it is.

definition.name: fusion_mcp_status
definition.description: Check Autodesk Fusion through the configured Fusion MCP server (fusion360-mcp-server, faust-machines or the pinned fork with document binding): whether it is configured, Fusion is running, the Fusion360MCP add-in answers on its port, and the server's tools and schemas. connected is true only when the add-in answers. With launch: true, starts Fusion on macOS when it is not running and waits up to 90 s for the add-in. Configure FUSION_MCP_COMMAND (uvx) and FUSION_MCP_ARGS (["--from","git+https://github.com/DMontgomery40/fusion360-mcp-server@86a3016a5a5b","fusion360-mcp-server","--mode","socket"]), or run fusion_mcp_setup.

launch.description: Start Autodesk Fusion (open -a "Autodesk Fusion") when it is not running, then wait up to 90 s for the add-in.

timeout_ms.description: Connection and discovery deadline in milliseconds; defaults to FUSION_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 180000.

connected.description: The Fusion MCP server started and the add-in answered its ping.

addinReachable.description: The Fusion360MCP add-in answered a ping on FUSION_MCP_HOST:FUSION_MCP_PORT (default localhost:9877) within 2 s. Another program on that port, such as Blender's MCP add-on, does not count.

activeDesign.description: When connected: whether Fusion has a design open, from the add-in's read-only get_design_type (false is its NO_ACTIVE_DESIGN). The pinned add-in refuses every design command, fusion_mcp_new_design included, without one (faust issue #12). Absent when unknown.

pin.description: The faust-machines/fusion360-mcp-server commit this bridge is set up for.

definition.name: get_printer_filaments
definition.description: Get the live AMS/external filament inventory from the printer over MQTT, including loaded/empty slot summary, resolved slicer profile paths, match confidence, and recommended load_filaments when the printer model is known.

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the printer (default: value from env)

bambu_serial.description: Serial number for the Bambu Lab printer (default: value from env)

bambu_token.description: Access token for the Bambu Lab printer (default: value from env)

bambu_model.description: Optional model hint used to resolve Bambu/Orca filament profile JSONs for each tray.

nozzle_diameter.description: Optional nozzle diameter used when resolving model-specific filament profile JSONs (default: 0.4).

definition.name: get_printer_status
definition.description: Get the current status of the Bambu Lab printer

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the printer (default: value from env)

bambu_serial.description: Serial number for the Bambu Lab printer (default: value from env)

bambu_token.description: Access token for the Bambu Lab printer (default: value from env)

definition.name: get_slice_settings
definition.description: Inspect slicer settings from a saved 3MF template or a JSON/config slicer profile without slicing anything. For a 3MF given as source_path, own_process is true when slice_stl, given this call's other arguments as it would take them (slicer_profile, template_name, template_3mf_path, layer_height, wall_loops, sparse_infill_density, quality, strength), prints the process the file carries (a designer's Bambu Studio or Orca project) unchanged. A 3MF with no slicer settings reports raw_key_count 0; a file that can't be read is an error.

source_path.description: Path to a 3MF template, extracted project_settings.config, or slicer profile JSON.

template_name.description: Optional named template from the local registry. Without source_path it is the source read; with source_path it is the slice's template, for own_process.

template_dir.description: Optional template directory override when resolving template_name.

slicer_profile.description: For own_process: the slicer_profile slice_stl would be given.

template_3mf_path.description: For own_process: the template_3mf_path slice_stl would be given.

layer_height.description: For own_process: the layer_height slice_stl would be given.

nozzle_diameter.description: For own_process: the nozzle_diameter slice_stl would be given; layer heights are checked against it.

wall_loops.description: For own_process: the wall_loops slice_stl would be given.

sparse_infill_density.description: For own_process: the sparse_infill_density slice_stl would be given.

enable_support.description: For own_process: the enable_support slice_stl would be given.

support_type.description: For own_process: the support_type slice_stl would be given.

quality.description: Print quality: draft (thicker layers, faster), standard (the preset's own layer height) or fine (thinner layers). The server picks the layer height for the nozzle in use; an explicit layer_height wins.

strength.description: Part strength: standard (the process's own walls and infill), strong or max (at least more walls and denser infill; a process that already has more keeps it). The server picks the values; explicit wall_loops or sparse_infill_density win.

definition.name: get_stl_info
definition.description: Get detailed information about an STL file (bounding box, face count, dimensions)

stl_path.description: Path to the STL file to analyze

definition.name: inspect_print_file
definition.description: Inspect an exact private snapshot of a prepared sliced 3MF or textual G-code file and selected plate without contacting a printer. Returns versioned file-only evidence; no printer readiness or permission to dispatch is established. Does not auto-slice.

file_path.description: Local prepared .3mf or textual .gcode artifact to inspect; checksum-only and unsliced projects reject.

bambu_model.description: Explicit file-inspection target model; never inferred from environment or live state.

plate_index.description: Zero-based selected plate; defaults to 0. Raw G-code only supports 0.

nozzle_diameters.description: Optional requested nozzle diameters to compare with file declarations; this does not observe installed hardware.

bed_type.description: Optional declared bed type to compare with file metadata.

include_preview.description: Also return preview: PNG pictures drawn from this exact file's G-code (every extruding line in its filament's colour; the top as it sits on the bed, and the bed side turned over), with the artifact's sha256. Large (tens of KB of base64); for apps that show the person what will print, not for agents.

definition.name: lay_flat
definition.description: Rotate the model so a face rests on the bed (Z=0), choosing the orientation with the least part and support volume per mm² of bed contact. A face counts only if nothing hangs below it. Returns the new STL path; structuredContent.laid_flat is false, with the input path, when no orientation qualifies.

definition.name: list_3mf_plate_objects
definition.description: List the objects of a sliced 3MF plate that the printer can skip, one per copy, as Bambu Studio's skip dialog lists them: identify_id (id), name, whether it is already skipped, and labelObjectEnabled (the plate was sliced with object labels, which skipping needs). Use these ids with skip_objects during a running print.

definition.name: list_3mf_plates
definition.description: List a Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer 3MF's plates as its designer laid them out, before slicing: plate_count, and for each plate its index (from 0; slice_stl's slice_plate is index + 1, inspect_print_file's plate_index is index), name, the objects on it, each object copy's identify_id (instances: the ids slice_stl's skip_objects takes) whether the file already holds its G-code (sliced), and filaments: the project filaments that plate prints with and only those (index from 1 = slice_stl's load_filaments/filament_colours position and print_3mf's ams_mapping position + 1; colour, material, filament_id, and the first part using it), from the slice when there is one, otherwise worked out as Bambu Studio does from the plate's parts, painting, support, layer ranges and tool changes. filaments_complete is false when a part's mesh was too large to read its painting: that plate then lists every declared filament, so offer them all rather than miss one that prints. project_filaments lists every filament the project declares, used or not (slice_stl takes one load_filaments profile per declared filament). A plain 3MF without plate metadata is one plate. include_thumbnails adds each plate's own preview from the file (thumbnail_png_base64). Read-only.

three_mf_path.description: Path to the 3MF (a designer's project, sliced or not)

include_thumbnails.description: Include each plate's own preview PNG from the file, base64 (default false)

definition.name: list_printer_files

host.description: Hostname or IP of the printer (default: value from env)

definition.name: list_templates
definition.description: List saved slicing templates from the local template registry directory.

template_dir.description: Optional template directory override. Defaults to BAMBU_TEMPLATE_DIR or the server's configured local template registry.

definition.name: merge_vertices
definition.description: Merge vertices in an STL file closer than the specified tolerance

definition.name: pause_print
definition.description: Pause the current print job on the Bambu Lab printer (resumable via resume_print)

host.description: Hostname or IP of the printer (default: value from env)

connection_mode.description: The connection the print used. Defaults to BAMBU_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_MODE, the same default print_3mf uses, else the model's route.

connection_type.description: FULU BambuNetwork connection type the print used. Defaults to BAMBU_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_TYPE, as for print_3mf. Authenticated controls support lan.

definition.name: print_3mf
definition.description: Print a 3MF file on a Bambu Lab printer. Auto-slices if the 3MF has no gcode. IMPORTANT: bambu_model must be specified to ensure safe printer operation.

three_mf_path.description: Path to the 3MF file to print

pause_at_layers.description: Pause before each of these layers (1-based, as Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer number them in the preview), for example to drop in magnets or nuts. The slicer writes the printer's own pause G-code there (M400 U1 on Bambu printers); the printer stops by itself and waits for Resume. Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer CLI only. Used when the 3MF has no G-code yet; a sliced 3MF must already carry these pauses, or it is refused.

bambu_model.description: REQUIRED: Bambu Lab printer model. Ask the user if not known. Using the wrong model can damage the printer.

connection_mode.description: Print path: bambu_connect hands a printable file to the signed-in Bambu Connect app for cloud-mode review; X2D otherwise defaults to bambu_native (Bambu Studio's installed local networking plug-in, storing the job on a ready SD card or USB stick, otherwise internal eMMC); lan_mqtt_ftps is the legacy direct MQTT/FTPS path; bambu_network uses the FULU bridge.

try_emmc_print.description: X2D native printing: true stores the job on internal storage (eMMC), false on the SD card or USB stick (refused unless the printer reports one ready). Omit to use the card when ready, else eMMC; BAMBU_NATIVE_TRY_EMMC_PRINT sets a server default.

connection_type.description: BambuNetwork connection type when connection_mode is bambu_network; cloud uses restored internet printing, lan uses local bridge printing.

bambu_network_method.description: FULU print method when connection_mode is bambu_network; defaults to start_local_print for lan, and for cloud to Bambu Studio's order: start_local_print_with_record, then start_print if that fails.

dev_id.description: Bambu device id for FULU BambuNetwork printing; defaults to BAMBU_DEV_ID or BAMBU_SERIAL.

dev_ip.description: Printer IP address for FULU BambuNetwork LAN/local print methods; defaults to host when provided.

bridge_command.description: Override command for the FULU bridge host or macOS/WSL wrapper; defaults to BAMBU_NETWORK_BRIDGE_COMMAND. Per-call overrides require MCP_ALLOW_EXECUTABLE_ARG=1.

bambu_network_config_dir.description: Config/log directory used by the FULU BambuNetwork agent.

country_code.description: BambuNetwork country code, such as US, used by the FULU bridge agent.

nozzle_volume_type.description: Installed nozzle flow type, used when the 3MF must be auto-sliced (default: BAMBU_NOZZLE_VOLUME_TYPE, else standard).

plate_index.description: Zero-based plate index to print from the sliced 3MF (default: 0)

slicer_type.description: Slicer to use only if auto-slicing an unsliced 3MF. Bambu-compatible slicer aliases such as fulu-orca and orca-studio are accepted.

use_ams.description: Whether to use the AMS (default: auto-detect from 3MF)

ams_mapping.description: Project-level AMS mapping array. Position = project filament index, value = absolute AMS tray. Positions the selected plate does not print are sent as -1, as Bambu Studio sends them, whatever is passed there (0-3=AMS 0, 4-7=AMS 1, 8-11=AMS 2, 128+=AMS-HT, 254=external, -1=unused). On dual-nozzle printers (H2D, H2D Pro, H2C, X2D) 254 is the LEFT/deputy nozzle external spool and 255 the RIGHT/main nozzle external spool, matching Bambu Studio's virtual tray ids; the gcode header's filament_map (1=left, 2=right) says which nozzle each filament was sliced for. Prefer ams_slots unless you know the project-level layout.

ams_slots.description: Preferred AMS input: one absolute tray index per USED filament in plate order, e.g. [1] for a single-filament print pulling from AMS 0 slot 1. Use 254 for the external spool (on dual-nozzle printers: 254 = left/deputy nozzle external, 255 = right/main nozzle external). Expanded to project-level ams_mapping automatically from the 3MF's plate_N.json and gcode header.

auto_match_ams.description: When true, match the sliced 3MF's tray_info_idx requirements against live AMS inventory and use the resulting ams_slots. Ignored when ams_mapping or ams_slots is provided.

bed_leveling.description: Auto bed leveling on or off. Omit to send what Bambu Studio's Send dialog would: the choice saved in BambuStudio.conf for this printer, else Studio's default.

flow_calibration.description: Flow calibration on or off. Omit to send what Bambu Studio's Send dialog would (auto on P1/P1S).

vibration_calibration.description: Vibration calibration (default false, as Bambu Studio sends).

template_name.description: Optional named template from the local registry. Resolves to template_3mf_path automatically.

template_dir.description: Optional template directory override when resolving template_name.

nozzle_diameters.description: Complete per-nozzle diameters for a pre-sliced job, e.g. [0.4, 0.6]. Omit to verify its declared diameters against live telemetry; cannot combine with nozzle_diameter.

use_ssl_for_ftp.description: Whether FULU local print should use SSL for FTP (default: true).

extra_options.description: Raw JSON string or text for FULU PrintParams extra_options.

definition.name: slice_stl
definition.description: Slice an STL or 3MF file using a slicer to generate printable G-code or sliced 3MF. IMPORTANT: bambu_model must be specified to ensure the slicer generates safe G-code for the correct printer. The text result is the sliced file's path. When Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer writes a result.json, structuredContent.slicer_result carries it verbatim, success or error: error_string, return_code and each sliced_plates[].warning_message, such as a floating cantilever. structuredContent.slicer_report says whether it failed; for a failure, its message is a plain sentence for a person and slicer_message keeps the slicer's words, which a failed slice's text gives after that sentence. A 3MF that carries its own process settings (a designer's Bambu Studio or Orca project) slices with them unless slicer_profile, template_name or template_3mf_path is given; the machine still comes from bambu_model. quality and strength adjust that process, and strength never lowers its walls or infill.

stl_path.description: Path to the STL or 3MF file to slice

bambu_model.description: REQUIRED: Bambu Lab printer model. Ask the user if not known. Using the wrong model can damage the printer.

slicer_type.description: Type of slicer to use. Bambu-compatible choices (bambustudio, orcaslicer, orcaslicer-bambulab) export sliced 3MF; aliases such as fulu-orca and orca-studio are accepted.

slicer_path.description: Path to the slicer executable (default: value from env). Per-call overrides require MCP_ALLOW_EXECUTABLE_ARG=1.

slicer_profile.description: Path to an optional process profile/config file. The exact bambu_model/nozzle machine preset is still required.

template_3mf_path.description: Optional template 3MF whose embedded Bambu slicer settings should be reused when slicing a new STL or 3MF.

template_name.description: Optional named template from the local registry. Resolves to template_3mf_path automatically.

template_dir.description: Optional template directory override when resolving template_name.

bed_type.description: Bed plate type for slicing (default: textured_plate).

nozzle_type.description: Bambu-compatible slicing: the hotend nozzle material installed on the printer (default: BAMBU_NOZZLE_TYPE, else the model preset's stock nozzle, usually stainless_steel). Printing compares it with the printer's reported nozzle.

nozzle_volume_type.description: Bambu-compatible slicing: the flow type of the nozzle installed on the printer (default: BAMBU_NOZZLE_VOLUME_TYPE, else standard). high_flow uses the presets' High Flow values, such as the filament's High Flow max volumetric speed, and is refused if the machine preset has no High Flow variant. Printing compares it with the printer's reported nozzle flow.

use_printer_filaments.description: When true, and no explicit slicer profile or load_filaments override is provided, use the printer's current or first loaded AMS filament as the slicer filament profile. Template 3MF process settings can still be used at the same time.

uptodate.description: Refresh 3MF preset configs to match the latest BambuStudio version. Use when slicing downloaded or older 3MF files to prevent stale-config failures.

repetitions.description: Slice N identical copies of the model. Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer copy an STL with --clone-objects; do not also pass clone_objects. Copies may need multiple plates; print_3mf prints one selected plate per call. For 3MF input, select slice_plate explicitly.

orient.description: Auto-orient the model for optimal printability (minimize supports, maximize bed adhesion). Recommended for raw STL imports that lack a pre-set orientation.

arrange.description: Auto-arrange all objects on the build plate with optimal spacing; STL input is arranged by default. Set false only to keep a 3MF's existing layout: an STL that is not already on the plate then fails to slice.

ensure_on_bed.description: Detect models floating above the bed and lower them onto the build surface. Safety net for imported models with incorrect Z origins.

clone_objects.description: Clone the loaded model: total copies as a single integer, e.g. '3'. The Bambu-style CLIs count copies per input file and this tool loads one file, so a comma-separated list is rejected by the slicer.

skip_objects.description: Skip these object copies when slicing, by identify_id, comma-separated (e.g. '78,92'). The ids are the instances list_3mf_plates gives for each plate; they are not positions. Useful for multi-object 3MFs where you only want to print some parts.

load_filaments.description: Override filament profiles. Semicolon-separated paths to filament JSON configs, e.g. 'pla_basic.json;petg_cf.json'.

filament_profile.description: Compatibility alias for load_filaments. Semicolon-separated Orca/Bambu filament profile JSON paths.

load_filament_ids.description: Map filaments to objects/parts. Comma-separated IDs matching load_filaments order, e.g. '1,2,3,1' assigns filament 1 to objects 0 and 3.

filament_colours.description: Optional slot colours, one #RRGGBB per filament slot in order, separated by ';' (e.g. '#161616;#FFFFFF'). Defaults to the input 3MF's project colours, else the BambuStudio default.

enable_timelapse.description: Insert timelapse parking moves into gcode. The toolhead parks at a fixed position each layer for camera capture. Adds ~10% print time.

allow_mix_temp.description: Allow filaments with different temperature requirements on the same plate. Required for multi-material prints mixing e.g. PLA and PETG.

scale.description: Uniform scale factor applied to all axes. 1.0 = original size, 2.0 = double, 0.5 = half. Applied before slicing.

rotate.description: Rotate the model around the Z-axis (vertical) by this many degrees before slicing. Positive = counterclockwise when viewed from above.

rotate_x.description: Rotate the model around the X-axis by this many degrees before slicing. Useful for reorienting prints for better layer adhesion.

rotate_y.description: Rotate the model around the Y-axis by this many degrees before slicing. Useful for reorienting prints for better layer adhesion.

min_save.description: Write a smaller output 3MF by omitting non-essential metadata. Reduces file size for faster FTP upload to the printer.

skip_modified_gcodes.description: Strip custom start/end gcodes embedded in the 3MF. Recommended for downloaded 3MFs since custom gcodes from other users' profiles may be unsafe for your printer.

pause_at_layers.description: Pause before each of these layers (1-based, as Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer number them in the preview), for example to drop in magnets or nuts. The slicer writes the printer's own pause G-code there (M400 U1 on Bambu printers); the printer stops by itself and waits for Resume. Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer CLI only. Pauses already in a project 3MF are kept.

slice_plate.description: Which plate index to slice. 0 = all plates for local slicers; remote slicing defaults to plate 1 and rejects 0. Use 1, 2, etc. to slice only a specific plate in multi-plate 3MF projects.

quality.description: Print quality: draft (thicker layers, faster), standard (the preset's own layer height) or fine (thinner layers). The server picks the layer height for the nozzle in use; an explicit layer_height wins.

strength.description: Part strength: standard (the process's own walls and infill), strong or max (at least more walls and denser infill; a process that already has more keeps it). The server picks the values; explicit wall_loops or sparse_infill_density win.

layer_height.description: Layer height in mm, such as 0.28 (draft), 0.2 (standard) or 0.12 (fine). Written as the process preset's layer_height over the machine and process preset this tool resolves; at most the nozzle diameter. Bambu-compatible slicers only.

wall_loops.description: Number of walls (perimeters), written as the process preset's wall_loops. Bambu-compatible slicers only.

sparse_infill_density.description: Sparse infill density as a percentage, such as "15%", written as the process preset's sparse_infill_density. Bambu-compatible slicers only.

enable_support.description: Turn support generation on or off, written as the process preset's enable_support. Bambu-compatible slicers only.

support_type.description: Support style, written as the process preset's support_type. Bambu-compatible slicers only.

support_threshold_angle.description: Overhang threshold in degrees for automatic supports, written as the process preset's support_threshold_angle (0 lets the slicer decide). Bambu-compatible slicers only.

slicer_type.description: Type of slicer to use. Bambu-compatible choices (bambustudio, orcaslicer, orcaslicer-bambulab) export sliced 3MF; aliases such as fulu-orca and orca-studio are accepted.

nozzle_type.description: Bambu-compatible slicing: the hotend nozzle material installed on the printer (default: BAMBU_NOZZLE_TYPE, else the model preset's stock nozzle, usually stainless_steel). Printing compares it with the printer's reported nozzle.

Printing compares it with the printer's reported nozzle flow.

ensure_on_bed.description: Lift floating models onto the bed.

arrange.description: Auto-arrange objects on the build plate.

repetitions.description: Total copies of an STL, using clone_objects internally. Do not also pass clone_objects. The slicer may place copies on multiple plates; print_3mf prints one selected plate per call. For 3MF input, select slice_plate explicitly.

The slicer writes the printer's own pause G-code there (M400 U1 on Bambu printers); the printer stops by itself and waits for Resume. Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer CLI only. Pauses already in a project 3MF are kept.

definition.name: bus_get_city_config
definition.title: Get city operating config
definition.description:
Get a city's runtime config: max poll interval and "arriving" time threshold.

This is mostly relevant if you are deciding how aggressively to refresh — not for end-user questions about lines or stops.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required): e.g. '034' (Shanghai), '027' (Beijing)
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "maxInterval": 30,
    "arrivingStationLimitSeconds": 180,
    "busDisplayConfig": { "lineDetail": "time#order#distance", "other": "time#order" }
  }

city_id.description: City ID, e.g. '034' for Shanghai, '027' for Beijing

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_line_detail
definition.title: Get full line detail (stops + live buses)
definition.description:
Full info for a line: rider-facing fields (name, first/last/price, stationsNum), the full ordered station list, the reverse-direction lineId, and every bus currently on the line.

**Use this — not bus_get_timetable — to answer "is line X still running" or "first/last bus time" questions.** The timetable tool only has data for a small minority of lines.

**Subway lines are NOT supported.** If bus_search returned a line with isSubway=true (e.g. lineId=1057 for 地铁2号线), this endpoint returns an empty payload — the response will carry `empty: true` and a `hint` field pointing at bus_get_nearby_stops / bus_plan_transit. Don't retry; route to those tools instead.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - line_id (string, required): from bus_search.lines[*].lineId
  - lat / lng (string, optional): caller's WGS-84 coordinates
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "line": { "lineId":"...", "name":"71", "lineNo":"r95817", "direction":0, "startSn":"...", "endSn":"...", "firstTime":"05:30", "lastTime":"23:30", "price":"2元", "stationsNum":24 },
    "stations": [{ "order":1, "sId":"...", "sn":"...", "wgsLat":..., "wgsLng":..., "physicalStId":"...", "namesakeStId":"...", "metros":[{"name":"地铁14号线","lineNo":"14号线","color":"97,96,32"}] }, ...],
    "buses": [{ "busId":"...", "order":2, "lat":..., "lng":..., "speed":5.7, "capacity":0, "distanceToWaitStn":...}],
    "reverseDirection": { "lineId":"...", "startSn":"...", "endSn":"...", "firstTime":"04:30", "lastTime":"22:30", "price":"2元" } | null,
    "depDesc": "...", "preArrivalTime": "...", "targetOrder": 24,
    "empty": true, "hint": "..."   // present only when upstream returned no data (subway / retired line)
  }

Each station carries:
- 'order' → feed into bus_get_line_realtime / bus_list_line_buses as target_order
- 'sId' → feed into bus_get_line_realtime as station_id (NOT into bus_get_stop_detail!)
- 'physicalStId' + 'namesakeStId' → feed into bus_get_stop_detail to see every line through that stop

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_line_realtime
definition.title: Get realtime buses for a (line, stop) pair
definition.description:
Canonical "when will my bus arrive" tool. Returns every bus currently on the line, with the nearest one carrying an ETA to the waiting stop.

**Important**: the upstream predicts an ETA for only the nearest bus heading to your stop. Buses farther up the route are returned (with position/speed/capacity) but their `eta` field is null. That's not a bug.

**Args**:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - line_id (string, required): from bus_search
  - target_order (string, required): the waiting stop's order on the line. Source: bus_get_line_detail.stations[i].order, or bus_get_nearby_stops.stops[].lines[].targetOrder.
  - station_id (string, required): sId of the waiting stop
  - lat / lng (string, required): WGS-84 — the user's location is best; if unavailable, use the waiting stop's wgsLat/wgsLng (from line_detail.stations[i]).
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "line": { "lineId":"...", "name":"71", "direction":0, "endSn":"..." },
    "targetOrder": 2,
    "realData": true,
    "buses": [
      { "busId":"...", "licence":"...", "order":2, "lat":..., "lng":..., "speed":5.7, "capacity":0, "distanceToWaitStn":90, "eta":{"travelTime":25,"arrivalTime":1779070466055,"displayTime":"10:14"} },
      { "busId":"...", "order":3, "lat":..., "lng":..., "speed":3, "capacity":0, "eta":null },
      ...
    ],
    "note": "..."
  }

Field notes:
- The 'line' sub-object intentionally omits startSn — upstream does not return it on this endpoint. Read it from bus_get_line_detail if needed.
- eta.travelTime is seconds remaining
- eta.arrivalTime is a ms timestamp
- eta.displayTime is a "HH:MM" hint from upstream
- capacity: 0=light, 1=moderate, 2=crowded

target_order.description: Order index of the waiting stop on the line. Get it from bus_get_line_detail.stations[].order or bus_get_nearby_stops.stops[].lines[].targetOrder.

lat.description: WGS-84 latitude. If the user's location is unknown, fall back to the waiting stop's lat (from line_detail.stations[].wgsLat).

lng.description: WGS-84 longitude. Fallback to the stop's wgsLng if unknown.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_line_route
definition.title: Get line polyline coordinates
definition.description:
Polyline coordinates for drawing a line on a map. Points with 'stopOrder' are actual stops; others are shape points between stops.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - line_id (string, required)
  - include_shape (boolean, default false): false returns only stop markers (~25 points); true returns all shape points (~400-500). Skip unless you actually need to draw the line.
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "pointCount": 480,           // total shape points upstream returned
    "stopCount": 23,             // stop markers among them
    "points": [{ "lat":..., "lng":..., "stopOrder":1 }, ...]
  }
'points' is the filtered list — stops only by default, full polyline when include_shape=true.

**Known caveat**: upstream sometimes omits the terminus stop from the polyline, so 'stopCount' may be one less than bus_get_line_detail's 'stationsNum' (e.g. 23 vs 24). Trust bus_get_line_detail for the authoritative station list; line_route is just for drawing.

Markdown mode only summarises counts; request JSON to read coordinates.

include_shape.description: If true, include all polyline shape points (often 400-500 per line). Default false returns only stop-marker points.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_my_location
definition.title: Get the caller's approximate location via IP
definition.description:
Resolve the caller's approximate location from their public IP — useful when the user asks something like "what's near me" without providing coordinates.

**Precision is city-level (typically a few kilometres).** Good enough to identify the city and seed bus_get_nearby_stops with a starting guess. NOT precise enough to find the user's actual bus stop — for that, ask for a landmark/address and resolve it via bus_search.

Caveats:
  - Resolves via ip-api.com (free tier; rate-limited but no auth).
  - VPN / corporate proxy → result reflects the proxy exit IP, not the user.
  - Cellular IPs often land on a provincial centroid.

Args:
  - ip (string, optional): a specific IPv4/IPv6 to look up. Omit to use the mcp server process's own outbound IP (= the caller's machine when running locally).
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "lat": 31.2222,
    "lng": 121.4581,
    "gpsType": "wgs",
    "city": "上海",
    "region": "上海市",
    "country": "中国",
    "ip": "116.236.0.1",
    "isp": "China Telecom",
    "precision": "city-level (~10 km); not suitable for stop-level queries"
  }

**Suggested workflow**:
  1. Call this tool to identify the user's city (match 'city' field against bus_list_cities to get a cityId).
  2. Pass lat/lng into bus_get_nearby_stops for a rough nearby list, OR ask the user to confirm a landmark and use bus_search.pois for sharper coordinates.

ip.description: Optional override IP to look up. Omit to use the mcp server's own outbound IP (i.e. the caller's machine).

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_get_nearby_stops
definition.title: Get nearby bus stops

limit.description: How many of the nearest stops to return. Default 5 — the upstream may return 15+ and most callers only care about the closest few.

definition.name: bus_get_stop_detail
definition.title: Get stop detail with all lines
definition.description:
Full detail for a stop: precise WGS-84 coordinates, every line that passes through (with first/last/price), realtime buses, and nearby metro lines.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - physical_st_id (string, required): from bus_get_nearby_stops / bus_search
  - namesake_st_id (string, optional): recommended; from the same source
  - first_line_id (string, optional): a line to highlight

Returns (json):
  {
    "stations": [
      { "sId": "...", "sn": "...", "lat": ..., "lng": ..., "distance": ...,
        "lines": [{ "lineId": "...", "name": "71", "direction": 0, "startSn": "...", "endSn": "...", "firstTime": "05:30", "lastTime": "23:30", "price": "2元", "targetOrder": 2, "buses": [...] }],

    ]

Multiple entries in stations[] mean the stop name maps to several physical platforms.

physical_st_id.description: physicalStId of the stop (from bus_get_nearby_stops or bus_search)

first_line_id.description: Optional hint of a line you want highlighted

definition.name: bus_get_timetable
definition.title: Get a line's per-trip schedule (rarely useful)
definition.description:
Per-trip departure schedule for a line. The upstream returns one of three modes via `mode`:
  - 'scheduled' (timeTableType=1): an explicit `timetable` array of trips
  - 'interval' (timeTableType=2): the line runs at a fixed headway — NO per-trip times are returned
  - 'special' / 'unknown' (timeTableType=3 or other)

**Most lines in Shanghai are 'interval'**, so this tool is rarely the right one. To answer "first/last bus", "is the line still running", or "what's the next departure", call **bus_get_line_detail** instead — it always returns firstTime / lastTime / price / live buses.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - line_id (string, required)
  - line_no (string, required): rider-facing short name from bus_search.lines[].name (e.g. '71'). Do NOT pass the internal lineNo like 'r95817'.
  - direction ('0'|'1'): the line direction
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "line": { "lineId":"...", "name":"71", "direction":0, "startSn":"...", "endSn":"..." },
    "timeTableType": 2,
    "mode": "interval",
    "timetable": null,
    "note": "This line runs at a fixed interval — ..."
  }

line_no.description: Rider-facing short name (search.lines[].name), e.g. '71'. NOT the internal lineNo like 'r95817'.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_list_cities
definition.title: List supported cities
definition.description:
List cities supported by the realtime bus data service.

Args:
  - hot_only (boolean, default true): return only the upstream's curated 'hot' set (~20 cities). Set false to dump the full ~480-city list (token-heavy, use sparingly).

Returns (json):

      ...
    ]

Use when: the user mentions a city name and you don't have its ID. The hot set covers the top-tier cities the user almost certainly means.

definition.name: bus_list_line_buses
definition.title: Get the nearest approaching bus on a line
definition.description:
Returns the nearest bus heading to the anchor stop, with ETA and the bus's next stop name.

**This is narrower than the name suggests.** Despite the upstream endpoint being called "busList", in practice it returns at most 1-2 buses (the imminent ones). For the FULL roster of every bus currently on the line, call **bus_get_line_detail** — its 'buses' array lists all live vehicles with positions.

Use this tool when you want a quick "what's about to arrive" answer for a specific stop.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - line_id (string, required)
  - target_order (string, required): the waiting stop's order on the line
  - station_name (string, required): display name of that anchor stop
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "targetOrder": 2,
    "buses": [
      { "busId":"...", "licence":"...", "order":2, "lat":..., "lng":..., "speed":8.2, "capacity":0, "nextStop":"西藏中路", "eta":{"travelTime":214,"arrivalTime":..., "displayTime":"10:14"} }
    ]
  }

station_name.description: Display name of the target stop

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

definition.name: bus_plan_transit
definition.title: Plan a public-transit route
definition.description:
Plan a public-transit (bus + metro) route between two points. Returns alternative plans sorted by recommendation, each broken into walking and ride segments.

**Coordinate system**: this tool expects GCJ-02. The easiest source is bus_search.pois[*].lat/lng — those are already GCJ-02 and carry a name. If you only have WGS-84 (e.g. from a phone GPS), convert it before calling.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required)
  - origin_name, origin_lat, origin_lng (string, required): origin in GCJ-02
  - dest_name, dest_lat, dest_lng (string, required): destination in GCJ-02
  - strategy ('0'|'1'|'2'|'3'): 0=recommended (default; surfaces metro), 1=fewest transfers, 2=least walking, 3=shortest time (BUS-ONLY — upstream often drops metro plans here, so for general "fastest route" questions use 0)
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "origin": "lng,lat",
    "destination": "lng,lat",
    "distance": 17982,
    "plans": [
      {
        "duration": 3056, "walkingDistance": 1466, "distance": 19086, "tag": "直达", "transitCount": 1,
        "segments": [
          { "type": "walking", "distance": 837, "duration": 717 },
          { "type": "bus", "name": "地铁2号线", "lineType": 1, "departureStop": "人民广场", "arrivalStop": "虹桥2号航站楼", "viaStops": 8, "duration": 1800, "distance": 17620, "startTime": "05:37", "endTime": "23:30" }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
lineType: 0=bus, 1=metro. Durations in seconds, distances in meters.

A top-level 'note' field is emitted when the response shape is suspicious — e.g. strategy=3 returned no metro plans despite this being a likely metro trip.

strategy.description: Routing strategy: 0=recommended (default; surfaces metro), 1=fewest transfers, 2=least walking, 3=shortest time among BUS-ONLY candidates (upstream often excludes metro from this strategy — when in doubt, use 0). For most user questions, 0 is the right choice.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

Returns (json):

    "province": "上海市",

definition.name: bus_search
definition.title: Search lines, stations, and POIs
definition.description:
Search inside a city by keyword. Returns matching lines, stations, and POIs in one call.

Use this as the primary entry point when the user gives a line number, station name, or destination name without IDs.

**Keyword tip**: plain "71", "71路", "地铁2号线", "陆家嘴" all work — the upstream is reasonably forgiving. If a short numeric returns empty, try appending "路".

**Coordinate systems**:
  - 'pois' coords are GCJ-02 (use directly with bus_plan_transit)
  - 'stations' coords are WGS-84 (use with bus_get_nearby_stops / bus_get_line_realtime)
  Both are also marked with a 'gpsType' field.

Args:
  - city_id (string, required): e.g. '034'
  - keyword (string, required)
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json')

Returns (json):
  {
    "highlightKey": "71路",
    "lines": [
      {
        "name": "71", "lineNo": "r95817", "isSubway": false,
        "directions": [
          { "direction": 0, "lineId": "21283603183", "startSn": "延安东路外滩", "endSn": "申昆路枢纽站" },
          { "direction": 1, "lineId": "21283603182", "startSn": "申昆路枢纽站", "endSn": "延安东路外滩" }
        ],
        // Compat top-level fields mirror directions[0] (or first available).
        "lineId": "21283603183", "direction": 0, "startSn": "延安东路外滩", "endSn": "申昆路枢纽站"
      },
      ...
    ],
    "stations": [{ "sId":"...", "sn":"西藏中路", "lat":31.231006, "lng":121.474316, "gpsType":"wgs", "physicalStId":"...", "namesakeStId":"...", "isSubway":false }, ...],
    "pois": [{ "name":"71路", "address":"...", "tag":"公交线路", "district":"黄浦区", "lat":31.233021, "lng":121.49073, "gpsType":"gcj" }, ...]
  }

**Line folding**: each entry in 'lines' is one logical line (e.g. "71路"). The two travel directions live in 'directions[]'. Pick the lineId matching your desired direction.

**Subway hint**: when 'isSubway' is true, the entry carries a 'hint' field — bus_get_line_detail will return empty for these lineIds. Use bus_get_stop_detail (metros field) or bus_plan_transit instead.

**Follow-ups**:
- directions[i].lineId → bus_get_line_detail (full stop list, first/last/price) — non-subway only
- stations[*].physicalStId + namesakeStId → bus_get_stop_detail
  (NOTE: a few stations lack physicalStId — typically metro-only entries with subwayV2=1. For those, use bus_get_nearby_stops to resolve the bus platform IDs nearby.)
- pois[*].lat/lng (GCJ) → bus_plan_transit as origin/destination

keyword.description: Search keyword. Examples: '71', '71路', '地铁2号线', '陆家嘴', '人民广场'. Plain line numbers like '71' work fine.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable text, 'json' for full structured data

Returns: same shape as bus_search but only the requested category is populated.

Retrieve matched CSS rules, inline styles (element.style), inherited styles, custom properties, and cascade wrappers (@layer, @media, @container, @scope) for an element identified by its UID.

Treat the output as authoritative and complete.
Results are paginated (10 rules per page by default); use pageIdx to page through the remaining rules. Requires a UID from take_snapshot.

definition.name: agent_execute
definition.description: Run a task on a previously-spawned agent_spawn record via the Anthropic Messages API with that agent's configured model. Use when native Task tool is wrong because (a) you need the spawned agent's persistent config (model, instructions, cost-tracking attribution) to apply to this turn, (b) the result needs to feed back into the agent's lifecycle (taskCount, lastResult, swarm-coordinated state), or (c) you want explicit model routing via the spawn record's `model` field instead of inheriting. For one-shot Claude prompts without a tracked agent, native Task is fine. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in env.

definition.name: agent_health
definition.description: Report measured agent_execute provider-call outcomes over the last 20 calls: API success-ratio health (0-1), error rate, and response-latency p50/p95. This does not measure task correctness. Agents with no observed calls have unknown health; registration is not proof of a running process. Native Task and hooks_post-task outcomes are not recorded here. Use when you need measured reliability for agents driven through agent_execute; native Task results are invisible to this tool, so inspect those directly.

definition.name: agent_list
definition.description: List every Ruflo-tracked agent in the registry with its type, model, status, and taskCount. Use when native Task tool is wrong because you need to see the swarm-wide agent inventory across turns (which agents exist, their roles, their cost-tracking handles) rather than spawn a new one-shot Task. Filter by status/domain/agentType if needed. For starting a fresh single-shot subagent, native Task is fine.

status.description: Filter by status (idle, busy, terminated; case-insensitive, aliases such as active/running/stopped). "all" or empty applies no status filter. Comma-separated values match any of them.

definition.name: agent_logs
definition.description: Return recorded activity-log entries for a tracked agent (idle/running history, last task result). Use when native Task tool is wrong because you need the agent's log across turns (what it did, last error/result, swarm context) rather than a one-shot Task transcript. For a Task you just ran, native Task output is fine. Pair with agent_list to find the agentId. (Hive-mind-spawned workers are resolved here too.) Today this returns the last task result as a synthetic entry — full per-agent activity logs land with hive worker execution wiring (ruvnet/ruflo#1916).

definition.name: agent_pool
definition.description: Manage a fixed-size warm pool of pre-spawned agents to skip cold-start cost on bursty workloads. Use when native Task is wrong because (a) you have a queue of similar tasks and want to amortize spawn latency, (b) cost-tracking wants stable agentIds across requests, or (c) swarm topology requires a known agent count at all times. For one-shot work, just call agent_spawn or native Task. Pool sizes and warm/idle thresholds are set per-pool.

targetSize.description: Target pool size (scale: grow or shrink to it; fill: grow to it, never shrink)

definition.name: agent_spawn
definition.description: Spawn a Ruflo-tracked agent with cost attribution + memory persistence + swarm coordination. Use when native Task tool is wrong because you need (a) cost tracking per agent in the cost-tracking namespace, (b) cross-session learning via the patterns namespace, or (c) coordination with other agents in a swarm topology (hierarchical / mesh / consensus). For one-shot subtasks with no learning loop, native Task is fine. Pair with hooks_route to pick the right model first.

agentType.description: Type of agent to spawn (a legacy `type` key is accepted as an alias)

name.description: Optional display name for the agent (shown by agent_list, agent_status and ruflo-console)

task.description: Task description for intelligent model routing

memoryBase.description: Opt-in: base .rvf memory file to fork a per-agent Copy-On-Write branch from (agenticow). When set, the agent gets an isolated ~162-byte COW branch instead of a full copy — promote on success, discard on terminate. Requires the optional `agenticow` dep; degrades to a no-op when absent or when CLAUDE_FLOW_NO_COW_MEMORY=1.

memoryDimension.description: Vector dimension for the COW base (required only when memoryBase does not exist yet)

definition.name: agent_status
definition.description: Read the lifecycle state of a single tracked agent: idle/running/stopped, current taskCount, lastResult, model, health score. Use when native Task tool is wrong because you need agent-level state (status across turns, accumulated taskCount, last error, swarm coordination) rather than a one-shot response. For inspecting a Task you just ran, native Task output is fine. Pair with agent_list to find the agentId first.

definition.name: agent_terminate
definition.description: Remove a Ruflo-tracked agent from the registry and free its swarm slot. Use when you need to (a) clean up a spawned agent so its cost-tracking row finalizes, (b) reclaim a swarm-topology slot for another agent, or (c) end a stuck agent without restarting the whole swarm. For one-shot Task tool invocations that already self-terminate, this tool is not needed. Pair with agent_list first to confirm the agentId.

promoteMemory.description: When the agent has a per-agent COW memory branch (spawned with memoryBase), promote (merge) its edits into the shared base on terminate. Default false → discard the branch (throw its edits away). No-op when the agent has no branch.

definition.name: agent_update

Use when native Task tool is wrong because the agent already has accumulated state (taskCount, swarm membership, cost-tracking attribution) and you only need to tweak one field — for example, promoting an idle agent to running on a new task, or rotating its model from haiku to sonnet mid-loop. For a brand-new subagent, agent_spawn (or native Task) is the right call.

For simple key-value persistence, memory_store/memory_retrieve are simpler. For unrelated file work, native Read/Write are fine.

definition.description: Record a causal edge between two memory entries via CausalMemoryGraph Use when generic memory_* tools are wrong because you need AgentDB-specific controllers (HNSW vector search, hierarchical tiers, causal-graph links, pattern store/recall, RaBitQ quantization). definition.name: agenticow_branch
definition.description: agenticow@~0.2.3 — COW-fork a base .rvf memory file. Measured 162-byte branches regardless of base size (verified at N=1k/10k/50k). Use when you need per-Darwin-iteration / per-user / per-session memory personalization. Copying the parent .rvf file is wrong because full-copy snapshots grow linearly (the 3.3 GB Darwin-worktree bloat fixed in v3.14.4); agenticow gives read-through semantics (parent ∪ edits, child wins) at constant 162 B. Optional dep — degrades to {degraded:true} when missing.

Use when you are about to run an experimental Darwin tick or speculative agent edit that may need to be discarded. Relying on the working node alone is wrong because there is no "undo last N writes" semantics — without a checkpoint, a bad ingest contaminates the base. Persists via .agenticow.json lineage manifest so it survives close+reopen.

Use when you are about to promote and want to preview the exact merge, or when auditing what a branch actually wrote. Diffing by re-querying is wrong because deletions (tombstones) are invisible to a read — diff() surfaces them explicitly. Requires the branch was opened with edit tracking (default on).

path.description: Path to branch .rvf file

definition.name: agenticow_ingest
definition.description: agenticow — write vectors (with optional text payloads) into an .rvf memory branch or base. Records: [{id?, vector, text?}] — id auto-assigns when omitted. This is the write half that makes a branch usable: agenticow_branch creates an empty COW child, but without ingest it has nothing to read back. Use when you have branched and must populate the branch (agenticow_branch alone leaves it empty). Editing the base directly is wrong when the writes are speculative — ingest into a branch, then promote only if validated. Persists via .agenticow.json lineage manifest.

path.description: Path to .rvf memory file (branch or base)

Use when you need branch history — to find checkpoint ids for a targeted rollback, or to debug a promote. Guessing the chain from filenames is wrong — lineage is the authoritative structure the store maintains.

path.description: Path to .rvf memory file

definition.name: agenticow_promote
definition.description: agenticow — merge a branch's edits back into its base (or an explicit target) memory file. After promote, branch edits become part of base lineage. Use when a per-user / per-Darwin-iteration branch has been validated and should graduate to shared memory (federation merge, A/B winner). Manually re-ingesting edits into the base is wrong because the edit set is opaque to the caller and tombstones (deletions) are easily missed; promote applies the full edit + tombstone set atomically.

definition.name: agenticow_query
definition.description: agenticow — k-NN read across an .rvf memory branch's full COW lineage (parent ∪ edits, child wins), returning {id, distance, branch, text}. Read-only (no manifest write). The `branch` field on each hit tells you which lineage node the result came from — the read-through semantics that make branching useful. Use when you need to read from an agent/session branch without materializing a full copy. Re-opening the base and manually merging edits is wrong: query already spans the chain (and uses the single-call Rust path when the branch was forked with nativeAnn).

path.description: Path to .rvf memory file

k.description: Number of nearest neighbors to return

definition.name: agenticow_rollback
definition.description: agenticow — discard all edits since the most recent checkpoint on an .rvf memory file. Reuses a fresh COW child derived from the checkpoint. Use when a Darwin tick or agent experiment regressed and you want to revert memory state without re-running. Deleting+rebuilding the .rvf is wrong because rebuild cost is O(N) and the data after the bad point is lost; rollback is O(edits-since-checkpoint) and the earlier history stays intact via the lineage manifest.

path.description: Path to .rvf memory file

definition.name: agenticow_speculate
definition.description: agenticow — speculative branch-and-promote for parallel A/B memory exploration. Forks a 162-byte COW branch per candidate off a shared base .rvf, ingests each candidate's vectors into its OWN isolated branch, scores every branch (probe-query 'nearest' distance or ingest 'count'), PROMOTES the winning branch's edits into base, and DISCARDS the losers by deleting their branch files. Use when you want to try N competing memory-write strategies and keep only the best — the memory-state analogue of worktree-per-agent code exploration. Copying the base per candidate is wrong (full-copy snapshots grow linearly, the 3.3 GB Darwin bloat); COW forks are constant-size and losers cost ~162 B to throw away. Optional dep — degrades to {degraded:true} when agenticow is missing.

scoreBy.description: 'nearest' = closest probe distance wins; 'count' = most accepted ingests wins. Default 'nearest'.

definition.name: business_pod_route_backend
definition.description: ADR-164 Phase 3 — Compute the domain-affinity routing decision for a business pod per ADR-164 §3.4 and return {backend, reason}. The three backends are local-stdio (preferLocalExecution=true), cloud-managed (preferLocalExecution=false AND budgetUsdMonthly >= 50), and remote-peer (everything else — small-budget non-local pods route through a federation peer node). Use when a /loop driver, @metaharness/router policy hook, or operator CLI needs the structural routing pick BEFORE the cost-optimal KRR step — surfacing this as an MCP tool keeps the rule auditable from the pod template alone and lets non-TS callers reach it. Re-implementing the rule in the caller is wrong because it forks the §3.4 source-of-truth and skips the {success,valid,error,path} envelope shape callers already rely on from business_pod_validate. Pair with business_pod_validate when pre-flighting a template, since this tool also runs full schema validation and degrades to the same error shape on malformed input. Threshold lives in CLOUD_BUDGET_THRESHOLD_USD in domain-affinity-policy.ts — keep that constant and this description aligned.

definition.name: business_pod_validate
definition.description: ADR-164 Phase 2 — Validate a business-pod template JSON against the schema in ADR-164 §3.3 (name, agents[], allowedMcpTools, bench, piiPolicy, budgets, cronSchedule, auditReadView, reservationExpiryMs bounded by ADR-164.1 §3.2). Use when a /loop driver or CI workflow needs to pre-flight a pod template before pod-tick.mjs reaches it — surfacing validation as JSON keeps the optional-dep degraded path clean. Hand-parsing the JSON in the caller is wrong because it skips the JSON-pointer error path and the reservationExpiryMs [5000, 300000] ms bound check that ADR-164.1 mandates. Pair with business_pod_validate -> pod-tick.mjs in the sales-pod smoke contract.
